items.definition_scope:
Definition / scope

Use for: Failures or errors during power-on and startup that prevent the device reaching a usable Windows desktop (or prevent successful login due to startup faults).

Includes:

No power / won’t turn on (no lights/fans, dead device) or powers on then immediately off

Boot loop / repeatedly restarting

Stuck at manufacturer logo (Dell/HP/Lenovo) / BIOS/POST screens, “Preparing Automatic Repair”

Windows won’t load (spinning dots forever), startup repair loops

Blue Screen (BSOD) occurring during boot

BitLocker recovery prompt (startup-related blocker)

“No boot device”, “Operating system not found”, boot device errors

Excludes:

Device reaches desktop but is slow/laggy/freezing (use Performance)

Display-only issues where the machine is running but screen output fails (use Display)

Password/MFA/account lockout at sign-in with normal boot (use Identity & Access)

Single application won’t open after login (use the app category)
items.playbook_steps:
Confirm the failure point (triage question):

Does it power on at all?

Does it reach logo/BIOS, Windows spinner, login screen, or desktop?

Any exact error text? (ask for a photo if needed)

Basic, safe actions:

If laptop: ensure charger connected; try a different power outlet/charger if available

Disconnect non-essential peripherals (USB drives, docks, external monitors) and retry

Force reboot sequence (as appropriate): power off fully, wait, power on again

If it reaches login screen but can’t sign in:

Check if it’s actually a credential issue vs boot issue (don’t keep under Bootup if it’s purely account-related)

If Windows is failing to load (repair/loop/BSOD):

Capture the exact BSOD stop code / error message and when it appears

Record whether it started after updates or a power outage

Route/escalate to the appropriate queue for OS recovery/reimage if standard checks fail

If “No boot device / OS not found”:

Treat as potentially urgent; likely disk/boot order failure → escalate for hands-on hardware/OS recovery

Evidence to capture (always):

Photo of error screen, device make/model, whether BitLocker recovery key is requested, recent changes (updates, drops, new hardware), and where it fails in the boot path.
keywords: “black screen on startup” (only if it’s truly boot-related

items.definition_scope:
Use for: Issues on an endpoint relating to local file/folder access and behaviour in Windows/File Explorer (or macOS Finder), where the problem is about files/folders themselves rather than an application/service being down.

Includes:

Can’t open/delete/rename/move/copy files or folders (e.g., “access denied”, “file in use”, “path too long”)

Missing or “disappearing” files/folders from the device (not clearly a cloud/service outage)

File Explorer crashes/hangs when browsing folders

Incorrect permissions on local folders, read-only behaviour on local paths

Corruption indicators (files won’t open, strange filenames, 0KB files) when it appears device/local-disk related

Excludes (route elsewhere):

SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams file issues, synced libraries, shared drives (use the relevant M365/Cloud Storage category)

Network drive mapping or access to file servers (use Network / File Shares)

Email attachments failing to open (use Email/Outlook)

Data recovery from deleted files / ransomware suspicion (use Security and escalate)

Requests to reorganise folders, create structures, or manage content (that’s a Request, not an incident)
items.playbook_steps:
Identify where the files live (decision point):

Ask: is the path local (e.g., C:\Users\...), OneDrive/SharePoint, or a network share (e.g., \\server\share / mapped drive)?

Clarify the failure mode:

What action fails (open/copy/move/delete/rename)? What exact error message?

One file vs many? One folder vs all folders?

Quick isolation / safe checks (local):

Confirm the file exists and the user has access to the path

Try from another location (Desktop vs Documents) / try a different file type

If “file in use”: close the related app, restart File Explorer, or reboot (if appropriate)

Check disk space and whether the path/filename is excessively long

If File Explorer is crashing/hanging:

Note whether it happens in a specific folder (could be a bad thumbnail/preview file)

Try accessing the folder via address bar path directly; disable preview pane as a quick test (optional)

If “access denied” on a local folder:

Confirm it’s not a protected system location

Capture the exact path and error; escalate if permissions ownership changes are required

Red flags (escalate as security/urgent):

Many files suddenly unreadable, renamed extensions, ransom notes, unusual shortcuts

Evidence to capture:

Exact file/folder path, error text, scope (# files), screenshots, whether it’s local vs OneDrive vs network, when it started, and any recent changes (sync client updates, profile changes, migrations).
keywords: “\server\share” / “mapped drive” (as a hint to exclude/reroute to network shares)

items.definition_scope:
Use for: Display output issues on laptops/desktops: no signal/black screen, external monitor not detected, flicker/tearing, wrong resolution/scaling, rotated display, brightness stuck, dock display issues.

Includes:

“No signal”, intermittent display loss

One monitor works, another doesn’t

External monitor/dock detection problems

Excludes:

Power/boot failure (won’t turn on, boot loop, stuck at BIOS/logo)

BSOD on startup

Single-application-only visual issues
items.playbook_steps:
Scope question: Is it internal screen, external, or both? Direct cable or via dock?

Isolation steps:

Reseat HDMI/DP; try different cable/port

Bypass the dock (connect direct if possible)

Confirm monitor input source

Windows quick checks: Win+P (project mode), detect/arrange displays.

Timeline check: Did it start after an update or new monitor/dock/cable?

Evidence: photos/screenshots of flicker patterns/errors; note which display path fails (dock vs direct).

items.definition_scope: Use for VPN client connection/auth issues that prevent access to internal resources from offsite. Includes: can’t connect, disconnects, DNS/internal resources unreachable only on VPN. Excludes: general internet down (ISP), Wi-Fi issues (WiFi item), account lockouts/MFA (Login Problem), application outage affecting on-site too.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm scope: user offsite? affects 1 or many? 2) Identify VPN type/client and exact error message. 3) Check internet works without VPN (browse a public site). 4) Quick isolation: try alternate network (mobile hotspot), bypass dock/ethernet, reboot. 5) Verify credentials/MFA prompts vs true tunnel failure. 6) Capture VPN logs/screenshots/error codes; note time of failure. Escalate if multiple users impacted or suspected service outage.

items.definition_scope: Use for failures to sign in to Windows/macOS or to the corporate account on the device. Includes: wrong password loops, account locked, MFA blocking sign-in, “user profile cannot be loaded”, repeated credential prompts at login. Excludes: device won’t boot to login screen (Bootup Problems), single-app sign-in (classify under app), network-only issues where cached login works but resources don’t (WiFi/VPN).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm where it fails: device login, domain/SSO prompt, or after login. 2) Check if user can sign in elsewhere (webmail/portal) to separate account vs device. 3) Ask exact message (photo). 4) If lockout suspected: verify identity per process, then unlock/reset as permitted. 5) If profile error: capture error text, check disk space, attempt safe reboot; escalate for profile repair if persists. 6) If MFA-related: confirm method/device time, retries, and whether other users affected.\

items.definition_scope: Use for integrated or USB camera not working in Windows/macOS or common apps. Includes: camera not detected, black screen, “camera in use”, poor quality only if device-level, privacy shutter issues. Excludes: app-specific permissions only (classify under app if clearly isolated), conference service outage, external device driver install requests (may be request depending on policy).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Scope: built-in vs USB webcam? one app or all apps? 2) Quick checks: privacy shutter/Fn key, cable/port swap for USB, unplug/replug. 3) OS checks: confirm camera permissions allowed; check if another app is using the camera; close Teams/Zoom/browser tabs. 4) Test in a second app (Camera app vs Teams) to isolate. 5) If device missing: check Device Manager/OS settings; note driver status (don’t deep-change unless allowed) and escalate if hardware suspected. 6) Capture: error text, app name, screenshots, device model.

items.definition_scope: Use for mouse/trackpad/trackpoint/touchpad issues affecting pointer control. Includes: cursor jumping, not moving, clicks not registering, scrolling issues, gestures not working if device-wide. Excludes: keyboard-only issues, touchscreen issues (if separate item), app-specific pointer issues (rare).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Identify device: touchpad vs external mouse vs both. 2) Quick isolation: if external mouse, change USB port / batteries / receiver; if touchpad, check Fn toggle key. 3) Check if issue is intermittent with movement/surface (for mouse). 4) OS settings: touchpad enabled, speed/gesture settings; test in safe basic context. 5) If both devices affected, consider OS lag/performance correlation and route accordingly. 6) Capture: device type, connection method, when it started, any recent

items.definition_scope: Use for wireless connectivity issues on the endpoint. Includes: can’t see SSID, can’t connect, frequent disconnects, poor signal, limited/no internet on Wi-Fi. Excludes: VPN-only internal access issues (VPN item), wired LAN issues (Network/LAN if you have it), service outages affecting everyone/site-wide (route as outage), password/MFA account lock issues (Login Problem)
items.playbook_steps: 1) Scope: is it only this device? only this location? home vs office? 2) Confirm symptoms: connected but no internet vs can’t connect vs drops. 3) Quick checks: toggle Wi-Fi, forget/reconnect network, reboot, move closer to AP/router. 4) Compare: does hotspot work? does ethernet work? do other devices work on same Wi-Fi? 5) Capture: SSID, error message, time, signal bars, IP status if known. Escalate if multiple users/site affected or AP suspected.

items.definition_scope:
Use for: The ticket indicates the device is not a supported/company asset or the asset/CI details are missing or wrong, meaning we can’t proceed with normal troubleshooting yet.

Includes: “personal device/BYOD”, “no asset tag”, “unknown device”, “not in CMDB”, “wrong device on ticket”.
items.playbook_steps:
Do not troubleshoot yet.

Ask for one identifier: asset tag or serial number or device name (hostname).

Route/escalate to the asset/CMDB correction process/queue (or whoever handles adding/fixing device records).

Once corrected, re-triage under the actual issue (Performance/Display/etc.).

items.definition_scope: Use for OS-level audio issues on a laptop/desktop: no sound output, mic/speaker not working, headset/dock audio not detected, wrong output/input device, crackling/distortion. Excludes app-only audio issues.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope: output, input, or both? Built-in vs headset/dock? Test in OS sound settings and one simple test (system sounds/voice recorder). Check correct input/output selected, mute/volume, reconnect headset/dock, try alternate port. Capture device type and any error. Escalate if multiple users or driver/hardware suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for email issues on a mobile device (can’t send/receive, sync issues, prompts to re-sign-in, missing mail on phone).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm device type and mail app. Check connectivity (wifi/mobile data). Ask whether mail works on another device/web. Basic: refresh mailbox, toggle airplane mode, re-open app, remove/re-add account only if approved. Capture error text and whether it’s one mailbox or multiple. Escalate if widespread or account-side issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for multi-factor authentication issues on mobile (approval prompts not received, codes not working, device change affecting MFA). Excludes password-only issues.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm what method is failing (push, code, SMS) and whether user changed phone. Check time/date on device, network connectivity, and whether prompts arrive. If locked out, follow approved identity verification and reset/re-enrol process. Capture exact error and affected services.

items.definition_scope: Use for collaboration app issues on mobile (can’t sign in, calls/meetings failing, notifications not working) where the problem is specific to mobile.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm if issue is sign-in, calling/meetings, chat, or notifications. Check app is up to date (if permitted), connectivity, permissions (mic/camera/notifications). Try sign out/in if approved. Capture error and whether it also happens on desktop/web.

items.definition_scope: Use for issues with the mobile device management (MDM) platform used by a specific customer (e.g., enrolment, compliance, app push).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm customer context and whether device is enrolled. Capture device details and the enrolment/compliance error. Basic: check connectivity, re-try enrolment steps per customer documentation. Escalate to the customer-specific MDM procedure/owner with evidence.

items.definition_scope: Use for mobile management/enrolment and compliance issues related to the organisation’s MDM/MAM policies (enrolment failures, compliance blocks, managed apps).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm whether issue is enrolment, compliance, or managed app access. Capture error text and when it occurs. Check connectivity and that user can sign in. Follow standard enrolment steps if documented; escalate if policy/compliance remediation is required.

items.definition_scope: Use for issues with the customer’s mobile-as-a-service provision (device supply/contract, swap/repair process) where it blocks the user.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm what is needed (replacement, SIM/service issue, device swap) and urgency. Gather device identifier and user details. Route to the agreed MaaS process/provider and keep user updated.

items.definition_scope: Use for Office productivity apps on a user’s desktop (won’t open, crashes, activation/licensing prompts, add-in problems).
items.playbook_steps: Identify which app(s) and whether issue is one user or many. Capture exact error. Basic: restart app, try safe mode if known/approved, check updates if permitted. Escalate if widespread licensing/activation or profile issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for an approved customer-specific business application delivered to desktops. Tier 1 must follow the available documented Tier-1 steps (e.g., in internal knowledge base) and should not guess.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm app name/customer, error, and steps to reproduce. Locate and follow the documented Tier‑1 instructions for this app. Capture screenshots/logs as specified. Escalate to application delivery/owner if instructions do not resolve or documentation is missing.

items.definition_scope: Use for other approved desktop applications not covered elsewhere (install/launch issues, crashes, functional errors).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm app name and whether it is approved/supported. Capture error and scope. Apply basic checks (restart, reinstall only if permitted, check updates). Escalate if app packaging/deployment issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for cloud sync client issues on desktop (not syncing, stuck syncing, sync errors, files not appearing locally).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm whether issue is desktop sync vs web access. Capture error text and affected path. Basic: pause/resume sync, restart client (if permitted), sign-in status, connectivity. Escalate if permissions/library or widespread service issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for browser issues on desktop (sites not loading, certificate errors, downloads blocked, browser crashing).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm whether one site or all sites and capture error. Basic: try private window, clear cache only if appropriate, test another browser if allowed. Escalate if policy/proxy restriction or widespread issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for collaboration app issues on desktop (sign-in, calling/meetings, chat, notifications) where desktop client is affected.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm which function fails and if mobile/web also affected. Capture error. Basic: restart app, check device settings for mic/camera, sign out/in if permitted. Escalate if multiple users or tenant-wide policy/outage suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for desktop email client issues (won’t open, crashing, search issues, profile prompts) excluding mailflow and spam routing.
items.playbook_steps: Capture exact symptom and error. Confirm if webmail works (to isolate client vs service). Basic: restart client, safe mode if approved, new profile only if documented. Escalate if widespread or mailbox/service issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for spam/junk mail issues (too much spam, legitimate mail going to junk, user reports phishing).
items.playbook_steps: Clarify: spam volume vs false positive vs phishing. For false positives, capture sender/subject/time and where it landed. For phishing, advise not to click and follow security reporting steps. Escalate per spam/phishing process.

items.definition_scope: Use for mail delivery problems (can’t send/receive, delays, bounce backs, NDRs) affecting one or more users.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm direction (inbound/outbound/internal), scope (one user vs many), and capture bounce/error text. Check if issue is limited to a domain/recipient. Escalate as mailflow incident if multiple users or system-level suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for mailbox/account access problems (locked out, password prompts, licence/mailbox not accessible) specific to email services.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm whether user can access webmail. Capture prompts/errors. If credentials/MFA, route to identity process as needed. Escalate if mailbox disabled/permission/licence required.

items.definition_scope: Use for issues with email groups (can’t send to group, not receiving group mail, membership issues impacting delivery).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm group name and symptom (send fails vs receive). Capture bounce/error and who is affected. Check if issue is membership/permissions vs mailflow. Escalate to messaging admin if changes required.

items.definition_scope: Use for webmail access issues (can’t log in to webmail, page errors, webmail missing features).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm if other services work and whether desktop client works. Capture error text/browser details. Basic: try private window, clear cache if appropriate. Escalate if service-wide or account-side issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Use for email signature problems (missing signature, wrong details, not applying). Excludes writing/designing signature content.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm whether signature is centrally managed or user-managed. If wrong details, correct source user details if permitted. If user-managed, show where to edit. If not applying for many users, escalate to email/signature service owner.

items.definition_scope: Use for backend email service issues affecting mailboxes (service errors, mailbox unavailable, widespread messaging faults).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope and symptoms. Capture errors and affected users. Check if multiple mail features impacted (send/receive, webmail, client). Escalate as service incident if widespread.

items.definition_scope: Use for email archiving/retention issues (missing archive, cannot access archive, archived mail not appearing).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm what is missing (archive mailbox vs specific items). Capture error and scope. Check whether issue is client vs web. Escalate to messaging/retention owner if policy change needed.

items.definition_scope: Use for printing issues to network printers (can’t print, printer offline, jobs stuck) from one or more devices.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope (one user vs many) and printer name/location. Basic: power cycle printer if on-site, clear queue, reconnect to printer, check network reachability. Capture error and job status. Escalate if printer/device down site-wide.

items.definition_scope: Use for multifunction device issues (printing + copying/scanning features failing, device errors).
items.playbook_steps: Capture device location and error code/message. Confirm which functions fail. Basic: reboot device if permitted, check paper/toner/jams. Escalate to support/provider with error codes and impact.

items.definition_scope: Use for scanning issues (scan to email/folder fails, scanner not detected, poor scan quality if device-level).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scan method (to email, to folder, to PC) and capture error. Check connectivity and destination availability. Basic: reboot device, re-try, verify destination path/account. Escalate if device config needed.

items.definition_scope: Use for printing via USB-connected printers (not detected, driver issues, jobs stuck) affecting a single device typically.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm printer is detected by OS. Try different USB port/cable. Restart print spooler if approved. Capture error. Escalate if driver/reinstall needed beyond Tier‑1.

items.definition_scope: Use for printing to a printer over Wi‑Fi (printer drops off network, can’t connect, intermittent).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm printer is on correct Wi‑Fi and has signal. Compare printing from another device. Basic: reconnect printer to Wi‑Fi (if on-site), power cycle, capture IP/SSID if available. Escalate if Wi‑Fi environment or printer networking suspected.

items.definition_scope: Resetting a user password when they cannot authenticate. If the user is blocked from working, treat as urgent. First establish authentication type (on‑prem directory vs cloud directory) using the customer site documentation (e.g., “Site Summary”).
items.playbook_steps: If blocking work, act immediately. 1) Verify identity per policy. 2) Check customer site documentation to confirm auth type (on‑prem vs cloud). 3) Perform the correct password reset procedure for that auth type. 4) Confirm user can sign in and update cached sessions if needed. 5) Record what was reset, time, and any follow-up (e.g., password change at next sign-in).

items.definition_scope: Unblocking/unlocking an account that is locked/blocked from authentication. If the user is blocked from working, treat as urgent. First establish authentication type (on‑prem directory vs cloud directory) using the customer site documentation (e.g., “Site Summary”).
items.playbook_steps: If blocking work, act immediately. 1) Verify identity per policy. 2) Confirm lockout/blocked status and auth type from site documentation. 3) Perform the correct unlock/unblock procedure for that auth type. 4) Confirm successful sign-in and advise on avoiding repeat lockout (e.g., old passwords on devices). 5) Document actions and any suspected cause.

items.definition_scope: Any suspected or confirmed security breach, most commonly account compromise. Requires immediate containment and escalation after initial securing steps.
items.playbook_steps: Treat as P1. 1) Capture key facts: who, what, when, suspicious activity indicators. 2) Secure the account using TSOP002 (per your SOP). 3) Confirm containment steps completed (e.g., credential reset, session revocation if in SOP). 4) Escalate to Tier 3 as P1 per workflow and include evidence/timeline. 5) Advise user on next steps per SOP.

items.definition_scope: Endpoints reporting or suspected to have virus/malware infection. #clarifysop
items.playbook_steps: 1) Instruct user to stop interacting with suspicious files/links; disconnect from network if policy says. 2) Gather symptoms and any alerts (screenshots, filenames, locations). 3) Run approved scan/containment steps per SOP and capture results. 4) Escalate if infection confirmed, spreading, or user is unable to work. 5) Document actions, indicators, and affected device details.

items.definition_scope: User needs multi-factor authentication reset/re-enrolment. Follow TSOP001.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Verify identity per policy. 2) Follow TSOP001 to reset/re-enrol MFA. 3) Confirm user can complete MFA registration and sign in. 4) Capture method used, time, and any errors encountered.

items.definition_scope: Security alerts raised by monitoring tooling (e.g., suspicious activity, endpoint detections). #clarifysop
items.playbook_steps: 1) Review alert details (severity, user/device, time, indicator). 2) Confirm whether it’s a true positive (ask for context, correlate with user activity). 3) Apply the relevant SOP for containment/investigation. 4) Escalate based on severity and scope; treat active compromise as P1. 5) Record indicators, actions taken, and outcome.

items.definition_scope: Wireless connectivity issues affecting a user/device or site (can’t connect, drops, weak signal, connected-no-internet). Excludes VPN-only/internal access issues.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope (one user vs many, home vs office). Capture SSID and error. Basic checks: toggle Wi‑Fi/airplane mode, forget/reconnect, reboot, move closer. Compare with another device or hotspot. Escalate if multiple users/site affected.

items.definition_scope: Network equipment issue impacting connectivity on a segment/site (LAN ports down, link down, intermittent local network).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm impact scope (which area/users). Check if issue is site-wide or segment-specific. Gather timestamps and affected locations. Check power/link lights if on-site hands available. Escalate to network team/provider with scope + symptoms.

items.definition_scope: Connectivity blocked or filtered by network security device/policy (sites/services blocked, new block after change).
items.playbook_steps: Identify what is blocked (destination, ports, internal/external) and who is affected. Confirm whether it worked before. Gather source site, destination, time. Escalate for rule/policy review if required.

items.definition_scope: Name resolution failures (sites/services unreachable by name but reachable by IP, “DNS server not responding”).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm symptom: name fails vs IP works. Capture failing domains and error. Basic checks: flush DNS cache (if permitted), reboot, test from another device/network. Escalate if multiple users affected or site-wide.

items.definition_scope: IP addressing issues from DHCP (no IP, APIPA/169.x, “can’t get IP”, frequent renewals).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm device has valid IP/gateway. Identify if one device or many. Basic checks: disconnect/reconnect, renew lease (if permitted), reboot. Escalate if multiple devices affected or scope exhaustion suspected.

items.definition_scope: Monitoring/alerts indicate a server is unreachable/unresponsive.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm alert details (host, time, last seen). Check for planned maintenance. Validate reachability if available. Determine if single server or multiple. Escalate as outage if confirmed offline.

items.definition_scope: A server-hosted application/service is failing or degraded (errors, service stopped, users can’t use app).
items.playbook_steps: Identify app, error, affected users, internal/external. Capture timestamps and recent change. Escalate to server/app owner with evidence.

items.definition_scope: Low disk space on a server causing alerts or failures.
items.playbook_steps: Capture drive/path and free space. Identify growth source if obvious (logs/temp). Only perform safe cleanup if approved; otherwise escalate. Confirm recovery after action.

items.definition_scope: Slowness/lag within a remote session/virtual desktop environment.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope (one user vs many) and whether local internet is stable. Capture time-of-day pattern. Basic: reconnect session, try different network if possible. Escalate if multiple users or host-level issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: File/folder access issues within a remote session (can’t open/move/delete, missing files in session context).
items.playbook_steps: Identify location (profile, redirected drive, shared location). Capture exact path and error. Check one file vs many. Escalate if storage/profile issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Display issues inside remote session (wrong resolution, scaling, multiple monitors, black screen in session).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm single vs multi-monitor, full screen vs windowed. Basic: reconnect, toggle full screen, adjust session display settings. Capture screenshots. Escalate if widespread.

items.definition_scope: Unable to log into remote desktop/session (auth failures, session stuck at sign-in, denied).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm where it fails (credentials vs connection). Check if user can sign in elsewhere. Capture exact message. Escalate if multiple users or broker/gateway issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Office apps within remote session failing (won’t open, activation prompts, crashes).
items.playbook_steps: Identify which app(s) and whether only in remote session. Capture exact error. Try one control test. Escalate to remote image/app owner if systemic.

items.definition_scope: Browser issues within remote session (sites not loading, errors, slow, downloads blocked).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm one site vs all sites and capture error. Check whether other apps reach internet. Basic cache reset only if appropriate. Escalate if policy restriction suspected.

items.definition_scope: Approved business application not working inside remote session.
items.playbook_steps: Capture app name, error, affected users, steps to reproduce. Confirm if it works outside remote environment (if applicable). Escalate to app owner with evidence.

items.definition_scope: General internet slowness/packet loss affecting browsing, video, or calls.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope (one user vs many, site vs home). Compare on another device/network; try wired vs wireless. Capture time pattern. Escalate if site-wide/provider suspected.

items.definition_scope: SharePoint slow loading, slow search, or sync delays affecting users.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope and location (site/library/page). Capture time and whether other cloud services impacted. Escalate if widespread.

items.definition_scope: Functional issues in SharePoint (access denied, can’t open files, missing libraries, errors).
items.playbook_steps: Identify site/library and error. Check permission vs outage. Confirm if others impacted. Escalate to platform admin/owner if permissions/config needed.

items.definition_scope: Removable storage not detected or read/write issues on the endpoint.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm device type and whether it works on another computer. Try different port. Check if blocked by policy. Capture error text. Escalate if policy restriction or hardware failure suspected.

items.definition_scope: Shared storage device inaccessible or degraded.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope and access method (path/mapped drive). Capture error and whether storage device is reachable. Escalate to storage/network owner if unavailable.

items.definition_scope: UPS alerts/faults affecting equipment power continuity.
items.playbook_steps: Capture alert text and location. Confirm what is connected and whether power event occurred. Escalate to facilities/on-site support/provider as appropriate.

items.definition_scope: Dictation/speech-to-text not working due to microphone/input selection or permissions (basic endpoint-level).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm mic works in general audio settings. Identify device (headset/built-in). Check input device selection and permissions. Escalate if application-specific beyond basic checks.

items.definition_scope: Ticket indicates device/CI is missing/incorrect/unsupported so troubleshooting can’t start yet.
items.playbook_steps: Don’t troubleshoot. Ask for one identifier (asset tag OR serial OR device name). Route for CI/asset correction. Re-triage once corrected.

items.definition_scope: Duplicate or related tickets that should be consolidated.
items.playbook_steps: Identify parent ticket and merge/relate per process. Keep communications on primary ticket. Close duplicates with reference.

items.definition_scope: Issue is no longer reproducible and appears to have self-resolved.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm with user service is restored and when. Capture what changed (time/reboot/network). Close with notes and advise to re-open if it returns.

items.definition_scope: Informational notification/alert with no stated impact (unless impact is described).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm if any user impact. If none, acknowledge and close or route as monitoring/admin task per process.

items.definition_scope: Work relates to a planned project/change rather than break/fix support.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm project name/owner/timeline. Route to project queue/team. Treat as incident only if it’s causing active service impact.

items.definition_scope: Doesn’t fit current incident taxonomy or lacks sufficient info to classify.
items.playbook_steps: Extract what’s known; ask up to 4 key questions; route to best-fit category once clarified.

items.definition_scope: Issue relates to an application outside supported scope.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm app name and need. If unsupported, advise and route/close per policy; if business critical, escalate for decision.

items.definition_scope: Issue is with an external vendor-managed service outside support responsibility.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm service name and impact. Check if widespread. Direct user to vendor route and document impact; escalate internally only if business critical.

items.definition_scope: Configuration/settings issues in Teams rather than an outage (notifications, devices, meeting settings).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm client type (desktop/web/mobile) and desired outcome. Provide basic guidance and gather screenshots. Escalate if tenant-wide policy changes needed.

items.definition_scope: User needs how-to guidance for an application rather than a fault.
items.playbook_steps: Clarify goal and blocker. Provide short steps or link to approved guide. If extensive, route to training/how-to process.

items.definition_scope: User needs how-to guidance for device/OS features rather than a fault.
items.playbook_steps: Clarify what they’re trying to do. Provide concise steps. If it becomes an error/failure, reclassify under the correct incident item.

items.definition_scope: Wireless connectivity issues affecting a user/device or site (can’t connect, drops, weak signal, connected-no-internet). Excludes VPN-only/internal access issues.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope (one user vs many, home vs office). Capture SSID and error. Basic checks: toggle Wi‑Fi/airplane mode, forget/reconnect, reboot, move closer. Compare with another device or hotspot. Escalate if multiple users/site affected.

items.definition_scope: Network equipment issue impacting connectivity on a segment/site (LAN ports down, link down, intermittent local network).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm impact scope (which area/users). Check if issue is site-wide or segment-specific. Gather timestamps and affected locations. Check power/link lights if on-site hands available. Escalate to network team/provider with scope + symptoms.

items.definition_scope: Connectivity blocked or filtered by network security device/policy (sites/services blocked, new block after change).
items.playbook_steps: Identify what is blocked (destination, ports, internal/external) and who is affected. Confirm whether it worked before. Gather source site, destination, time. Escalate for rule/policy review if required.

items.definition_scope: Name resolution failures (sites/services unreachable by name but reachable by IP, “DNS server not responding”).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm symptom: name fails vs IP works. Capture failing domains and error. Basic checks: flush DNS cache (if permitted), reboot, test from another device/network. Escalate if multiple users affected or site-wide.

items.definition_scope: IP addressing issues from DHCP (no IP, APIPA/169.x, “can’t get IP”, frequent renewals).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm device has valid IP/gateway. Identify if one device or many. Basic checks: disconnect/reconnect, renew lease (if permitted), reboot. Escalate if multiple devices affected or scope exhaustion suspected.

items.definition_scope: Monitoring/alerts indicate a server is unreachable/unresponsive.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm alert details (host, time, last seen). Check for planned maintenance. Validate reachability if available. Determine if single server or multiple. Escalate as outage if confirmed offline.

items.definition_scope: A server-hosted application/service is failing or degraded (errors, service stopped, users can’t use app).
items.playbook_steps: Identify app, error, affected users, internal/external. Capture timestamps and recent change. Escalate to server/app owner with evidence.

items.definition_scope: Low disk space on a server causing alerts or failures.
items.playbook_steps: Capture drive/path and free space. Identify growth source if obvious (logs/temp). Only perform safe cleanup if approved; otherwise escalate. Confirm recovery after action.

items.definition_scope: Slowness/lag within a remote session/virtual desktop environment.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope (one user vs many) and whether local internet is stable. Capture time-of-day pattern. Basic: reconnect session, try different network if possible. Escalate if multiple users or host-level issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: File/folder access issues within a remote session (can’t open/move/delete, missing files in session context).
items.playbook_steps: Identify location (profile, redirected drive, shared location). Capture exact path and error. Check one file vs many. Escalate if storage/profile issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Display issues inside remote session (wrong resolution, scaling, multiple monitors, black screen in session).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm single vs multi-monitor, full screen vs windowed. Basic: reconnect, toggle full screen, adjust session display settings. Capture screenshots. Escalate if widespread.

items.definition_scope: Unable to log into remote desktop/session (auth failures, session stuck at sign-in, denied).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm where it fails (credentials vs connection). Check if user can sign in elsewhere. Capture exact message. Escalate if multiple users or broker/gateway issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Office apps within remote session failing (won’t open, activation prompts, crashes).
items.playbook_steps: Identify which app(s) and whether only in remote session. Capture exact error. Try one control test. Escalate to remote image/app owner if systemic.

items.definition_scope: Browser issues within remote session (sites not loading, errors, slow, downloads blocked).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm one site vs all sites and capture error. Check whether other apps reach internet. Basic cache reset only if appropriate. Escalate if policy restriction suspected.

items.definition_scope: Approved business application not working inside remote session.
items.playbook_steps: Capture app name, error, affected users, steps to reproduce. Confirm if it works outside remote environment (if applicable). Escalate to app owner with evidence.

items.definition_scope: General internet slowness/packet loss affecting browsing, video, or calls.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope (one user vs many, site vs home). Compare on another device/network; try wired vs wireless. Capture time pattern. Escalate if site-wide/provider suspected.

items.definition_scope: SharePoint slow loading, slow search, or sync delays affecting users.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope and location (site/library/page). Capture time and whether other cloud services impacted. Escalate if widespread.

items.definition_scope: Functional issues in SharePoint (access denied, can’t open files, missing libraries, errors).
items.playbook_steps: Identify site/library and error. Check permission vs outage. Confirm if others impacted. Escalate to platform admin/owner if permissions/config needed.

items.definition_scope: Removable storage not detected or read/write issues on the endpoint.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm device type and whether it works on another computer. Try different port. Check if blocked by policy. Capture error text. Escalate if policy restriction or hardware failure suspected.

items.definition_scope: Shared storage device inaccessible or degraded.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm scope and access method (path/mapped drive). Capture error and whether storage device is reachable. Escalate to storage/network owner if unavailable.

items.definition_scope: UPS alerts/faults affecting equipment power continuity.
items.playbook_steps: Capture alert text and location. Confirm what is connected and whether power event occurred. Escalate to facilities/on-site support/provider as appropriate.

items.definition_scope: Dictation/speech-to-text not working due to microphone/input selection or permissions (basic endpoint-level).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm mic works in general audio settings. Identify device (headset/built-in). Check input device selection and permissions. Escalate if application-specific beyond basic checks.

items.definition_scope: Ticket indicates device/CI is missing/incorrect/unsupported so troubleshooting can’t start yet.
items.playbook_steps: Don’t troubleshoot. Ask for one identifier (asset tag OR serial OR device name). Route for CI/asset correction. Re-triage once corrected.

items.definition_scope: Duplicate or related tickets that should be consolidated.
items.playbook_steps: Identify parent ticket and merge/relate per process. Keep communications on primary ticket. Close duplicates with reference.

items.definition_scope: Issue is no longer reproducible and appears to have self-resolved.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm with user service is restored and when. Capture what changed (time/reboot/network). Close with notes and advise to re-open if it returns.

items.definition_scope: Informational notification/alert with no stated impact (unless impact is described).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm if any user impact. If none, acknowledge and close or route as monitoring/admin task per process.

items.definition_scope: Work relates to a planned project/change rather than break/fix support.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm project name/owner/timeline. Route to project queue/team. Treat as incident only if it’s causing active service impact.

items.definition_scope: Doesn’t fit current incident taxonomy or lacks sufficient info to classify.
items.playbook_steps: Extract what’s known; ask up to 4 key questions; route to best-fit category once clarified.

items.definition_scope: Issue relates to an application outside supported scope.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm app name and need. If unsupported, advise and route/close per policy; if business critical, escalate for decision.

items.definition_scope: Issue is with an external vendor-managed service outside support responsibility.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm service name and impact. Check if widespread. Direct user to vendor route and document impact; escalate internally only if business critical.

items.definition_scope: Configuration/settings issues in a collaboration app rather than an outage (notifications, devices, meeting settings).
items.playbook_steps: Confirm client type (desktop/web/mobile) and desired outcome. Provide basic guidance and gather screenshots. Escalate if tenant-wide policy changes needed.

items.definition_scope: User needs how-to guidance for an application rather than a fault.
items.playbook_steps: Clarify goal and blocker. Provide short steps or link to approved guide. If extensive, route to training/how-to process.

items.definition_scope: User needs how-to guidance for device/OS features rather than a fault.
items.playbook_steps: Clarify what they’re trying to do. Provide concise steps. If it becomes an error/failure, reclassify under the correct incident item.

items.definition_scope: File/folder issues in the cloud sync context (missing files, sync conflicts, can’t open from synced folder, errors syncing). Excludes purely local file issues.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm whether issue is in synced folder vs web portal. Capture exact error text and file path. Check if it affects one file or many. Basic: pause/resume sync, restart client (if permitted), verify user is signed in and has network. Escalate if widespread or permissions/library issue suspected.

items.definition_scope: Alert indicating a server is offline/unreachable (monitoring-driven).
items.playbook_steps: Capture host name, time, and alert source. Check for maintenance. Validate reachability if possible. If confirmed offline, treat as outage and escalate with scope (single vs multiple).

items.definition_scope: Alert indicating low disk space on a server or critical system.
items.playbook_steps: Capture affected host/drive and free space. Identify rapid growth if obvious. Perform only approved safe cleanup; otherwise escalate to system owner. Confirm alert clears after action.

items.definition_scope: Ticket indicates device/CI is missing/incorrect/unsupported so work cannot proceed yet (unsupported asset).
items.playbook_steps: Don’t troubleshoot. Ask for one identifier (asset tag OR serial OR device name). Route for CI/asset correction and re-triage once corrected.

items.definition_scope: Issue relates to an application outside supported scope.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm app name and need. If unsupported, advise and route/close per policy; if business critical, escalate for decision.

items.definition_scope: Issue is with an external vendor-managed service outside support responsibility.
items.playbook_steps: Confirm service name and impact. Check if widespread. Direct user to vendor route and document impact; escalate internally only if business critical.

items.escalation_guidance: This is a Tier 2 request

items.escalation_guidance: This is a Tier 2 request

items.escalation_guidance: This is a Tier 2 request

It is usually '3rd Party Support access', to install software, 'desktop app' or to update an application.   For update an application, we need to check whether it is automatically updated by Ninja 3rd party patching which is preferable to manually having to update everytime they need an update #clarifysop

items.escalation_guidance: This is a Tier 2 request

items.definition_scope: This is a T2 request unless there is client specific documentation that stipulates T1 can do it. #clarifysop
items.escalation_guidance: This is a Tier 2 request

items.definition_scope: Requests relating to email distribution groups (mailing lists) such as adding/removing members, changing owners, delivery permissions (who can send), or issues with access to manage the group. Tier 1 request.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm group name/address and what change is needed (add/remove member, owner change, send permissions, delivery settings). 2) Confirm required approval if policy requires it (e.g., group owner/POC). If missing, request it (do not escalate). 3) Apply the change using the standard group management procedure. 4) Confirm outcome (membership updated / sender can send / recipients receiving) and document exactly what changed.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 only if the group cannot be located/managed by Tier 1, changes fail repeatedly, request is outside standard SOP (complex restrictions/routing), or there’s a suspected mailflow/system issue impacting multiple users.

items.definition_scope:
Use for: Requests/issues related to email signatures (missing signature, incorrect details, signature not applying, inconsistency across devices).

Excludes / boundaries:

Do not write/design/format signature content (no bespoke layouts, marketing copy, image formatting).

Provide guidance and/or correct source data where appropriate.
items.playbook_steps: Determine whether whether the customer has Exclaimer or just uses native Outlook Signatures.

items.definition_scope: Requests to set or manage Out of Office/automatic replies. Ideally user enables themselves, but includes cases where user is away/no mailbox access or needs a specific auto-reply on a mailbox. Tier 1 request. #clarifysop
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm mailbox and required auto-reply details (internal vs external message, start/end, contact info). 2) If user can self-serve, guide them; if they cannot access mailbox, proceed per SOP. 3) Apply auto-reply and confirm it’s active. 4) Document exact wording and dates set.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 only if the SOP is unclear/not working, permissions prevent completion, or request involves complex mailbox scenarios not covered.

items.definition_scope: Requests for creation of shared mailboxes. Tier 2 request.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Gather requirements: mailbox name/address, owners, members, permission level(s), naming convention. 2) Confirm any required approval per client policy. 3) Route to Tier 2 with complete requirements to action.
items.escalation_guidance: Route to Tier 2 (default). Request missing info/approval first if needed.

items.definition_scope: Requests relating to mailbox archiving/retention. Must follow company policy and client-specific procedure in IT Glue. Procedure defines Tier 1 vs Tier 2. If no procedure exists, it is Tier 2.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Check IT Glue for the client archiving policy/procedure. 2) If procedure exists: follow it and route to Tier specified. 3) If no procedure: route to Tier 2 and record business requirement (who/what/why/when).
items.escalation_guidance: Tier depends on IT Glue procedure. If no procedure → Tier 2. If procedure unclear/not working → Tier 2.

items.definition_scope: Setup email on a mobile/tablet. Requires POC approval. Client-specific policy/procedure in IT Glue defines Tier (1 or 2) and any device management requirements.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm POC approval is present; if not, request it (do not escalate). 2) Check IT Glue for client mobile email policy/procedure (Tier, prerequisites, device management requirements). 3) Follow the documented procedure. 4) Record device type/OS and successful sign-in/sync.
items.escalation_guidance: Route/escalate based on IT Glue (Tier 1 or Tier 2). Escalate to Tier 2 if policy/procedure is missing/unclear or steps are blocked.

items.definition_scope: Calendar requests (shared calendars, access to another user’s calendar). Requires POC approval. Tier 1 request.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm POC approval is present; if not, request it (do not escalate). 2) Gather: whose calendar, who needs access, permission level, delegate vs view-only. 3) Apply access per SOP and confirm. 4) Document permissions granted.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 only if the documented method fails or scenario is not covered by SOP.

items.definition_scope: Requests to allowlist in spam filtering. Prefer customer self-service allowlisting where available; generally allowlist domains company-wide rather than individual addresses.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm what should be allowlisted (sender address vs domain) and whether it’s one-off or ongoing. 2) Encourage self-service allowlisting where available; provide instructions. 3) If IT action required: apply allowlisting per policy (prefer domain). 4) Record what was allowlisted and scope.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if allowlisting requires higher permissions, the request is high-risk/suspicious, or policy requires security review.

items.definition_scope: Requests for email forwarding rules. Requires POC approval. Tier 1 request. Removal must be a separate ticket (do not keep tickets open for scheduled removal). #clarifySOP
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm POC approval is present; if not, request it (do not escalate). 2) Gather: source mailbox, destination, keep-copy yes/no, start time. 3) Implement forwarding per SOP. 4) Advise that removal requires a new ticket and close upon completion.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 only if forwarding is blocked by policy/controls or Tier 1 cannot complete via SOP.

items.definition_scope: Customer reports a contact name needs changing or is incorrect. Tier 1 request.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm where the contact exists (personal vs shared/company directory). 2) Gather corrected details required. 3) Update via approved method and confirm with requester.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if it requires directory-level changes not permitted to Tier 1 or ownership is unclear.

items.definition_scope: Requests access to another mailbox. Needs POC approval. Tier 1 request.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm POC approval is present; if not, request it (do not escalate). 2) Gather: mailbox, requestor, access level (full access / send as / send on behalf). 3) Apply permissions per SOP and confirm. 4) Document exactly what was granted.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 only if SOP steps fail or request is not covered by the SOP.

items.item: Standard (Should Be Installed On Every PC)
items.definition_scope: Software install request where the application is listed in IT Glue as Standard for that customer (should be on every machine).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Check IT Glue approved applications list for the customer and confirm the app is classed as Standard. 2) Install/deploy using the standard method. 3) Confirm app opens/works. 4) Document device and outcome.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if the app isn’t listed as Standard, the install method is missing, or install repeatedly fails.

items.definition_scope: Software install request where the application is listed in IT Glue as Selective for that customer (installable on request).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Check IT Glue approved applications list and confirm Selective classification. 2) Confirm any required approvals if noted in IT Glue. 3) Install using standard method and confirm success. 4) Document.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if approval is required but missing, the app isn’t listed, or install method fails/is unavailable.

items.definition_scope: Software install request where IT Glue shows the app as Approval Needed for that customer (must obtain customer approver approval).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Check IT Glue approved applications list and confirm it’s Approval Needed. 2) Obtain the required customer approval (do not proceed without it). 3) Once approved, install via standard method or route if packaging is required. 4) Document approval evidence and outcome.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if approval route is unclear, the app needs packaging/deployment work, or install cannot be completed by Tier 1.

items.definition_scope: Customer requests a computer retired. Use TSOP0052. TSOP performs factory reset if device is endpoint-management enrolled; if not enrolled, TSOP won’t factory reset.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm device identifiers and retirement authorisation. 2) Follow TSOP0052. 3) If enrolled: perform factory reset per SOP; if not enrolled: follow SOP’s non-enrolled path/next step. 4) Update asset status and document outcome.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if device is not enrolled and TSOP does not cover next steps, or if reset/wipe fails.

items.definition_scope: User requests access to a printer. A printer CI should exist; if it does, Tier 1 can action. If not, it’s Tier 2.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm printer name/location and user/device. 2) Check for printer CI. 3) If CI exists: add/configure and confirm test print. 4) If no CI: route to Tier 2 for CI creation/validation and setup.
items.escalation_guidance: Route to Tier 2 if no CI exists or printer details cannot be validated.

items.definition_scope: Retire a computer for Crescent.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm device identifiers and retirement authorisation for Crescent. 2) Follow Crescent retirement procedure (or TSOP0052 if that is the defined method). 3) Update asset status and document outcome.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if procedure is missing/unclear or wipe/reset cannot be completed.

items.definition_scope: Customer request to remove a user profile from a computer. This is not performed routinely on leavers or device changes. Connexion policy is to manage profile cleanup via disk space monitoring alerts using SOPs (Tier 1: TSOP005, Tier 2: TSOP006), to preserve the ability to recover user data if needed.
items.playbook_steps: Explain Connexion policy: profiles are normally removed only via disk space remediation SOPs triggered by monitoring. 2) Check whether there is an active disk space alert; if so, follow TSOP005 or route per SOP. 3) If the customer still explicitly requests profile removal, confirm the user profile name and device and that no data recovery is required. 4) Remove the profile using the “Remove User Profile” script from Ninja. 5) Document customer confirmation and actions taken.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if: the profile removal script fails; the device is not accessible; multiple profiles require assessment; there is uncertainty about data retention/recovery; or the request conflicts with active disk space SOPs.

items.definition_scope: User name is incorrect or has changed. Tier 1 can action. Must check which service provides identity management (per Site Summary in IT Glue).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm correct new name and any required attributes. 2) Check IT Glue Site Summary to identify identity source (on‑prem vs cloud). 3) Follow the relevant name-change procedure for that identity source. 4) Confirm changes and advise on propagation/sign-out-in as needed.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if identity source/procedure is unclear, required permissions are missing, or changes cause downstream issues not covered by SOP.

items.definition_scope: Add a user to an address book on a company printer
items.playbook_steps: Followup procedure for client if exists.  If no procedure, then find instructions online
items.escalation_guidance: Tier 1 can do with or without a procedure as long as it is a supported CI

items.escalation_guidance: This is  a T1 procedure only Escalate to Tier 2 if documentation is missing/unclear.

items.escalation_guidance: This is  a T1 procedure only Escalate to Tier 2 if documentation is missing/unclear.

items.definition_scope: Use when processing multiple leavers in one request (bulk cleanup), typically where leavers occurred previously and the client notified late. Uses the generic batch-leaver SOP and is a shortened process vs the standard leaver SOP.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Confirm it is a batch request and obtain the full leaver list. 2) Capture effective leave dates (or confirm unknown/approx). 3) Run the generic Batch Leavers SOP checklist for each user (shortened steps). 4) Record actions per user and note any exceptions. 5) Provide a completion summary (processed / exceptions / unable to process).
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 if: any required step is unclear/blocked; exceptions are needed (VIP, shared mailbox owner, unusual access); mailbox/retention/legal-hold decisions are required; or tooling/permissions prevent completion.

items.definition_scope: Use for leaver requests where the current “new format” leaver procedure is available for Tier 1 to complete (procedure located in Monday).
items.playbook_steps: 1) Check for a completed leaver submission (form/portal). If missing/incomplete: request customer completion (do not escalate). 2) Locate the leaver SOP in Monday. 3) Follow the SOP exactly and record completion notes/evidence.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 only if you hit a snag: steps are unclear, documentation appears wrong/outdated, or the documented steps do not work.

items.definition_scope: Use for clients still on the old leaver procedure (not in new format / not suitable for Tier 1 completion). Primary intent is routing to Tier 2.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Check for a completed leaver submission (form/portal). If missing/incomplete: request customer completion (do not escalate). 2) If present: attach/link submission to the ticket and route to Tier 2 for completion using the old procedure.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 by default (once a valid leaver submission exists).

items.definition_scope: Use for temporary leaver requests (maternity leave, sabbatical, long-term leave) where the account should not be fully closed. Follows a generic temporary-leaver SOP and can be completed by Tier 1.
items.playbook_steps: 1) Check for a completed leaver submission (form/portal) stating temporary leave and dates/return info. If missing/incomplete: request customer completion (do not escalate). 2) Follow the generic Temporary Leaver SOP and record what was disabled vs retained.
items.escalation_guidance: Escalate to Tier 2 only if you hit a snag: the generic SOP is unclear, the documented steps don’t work, or the request includes exceptions not covered by the SOP.
